issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal):boolean (a boolean return type), but the template and the reference solution implement/add the method as a void method (template expects students to addAnimal(Animal) without a return, and solution has public void addAnimal(Animal)). This mismatch between the UML and the code/textual description can confuse students about the correct method signature and may cause compile/test failures if they follow the UML instead of the text/template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either change the UML in the problem statement to show addAnimal(animal: Animal):void to match the textual description and the template/solution, or modify the template and solution to implement addAnimal returning boolean (and document what the boolean indicates, e.g., success). Preferably update the UML to void to align with the task wording and the reference implementation.
